ec:2022:q15.title: GATE EC 2022 | Set 1 | Question: 15
ec:2022:q15.question:
Consider the following partial differential equation (PDE)
$a\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial x^2} +b\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial y^2}=f(x,y)$
, where $a$and $b$ are distinct positive real numbers. Select the combination(s) of values of the real parameters $\xi$ and $\eta$ such that $f(x,y)=e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}$ is a solution of the given PDE.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given

$$\begin{aligned}

f(x,y)&=e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}\\

\frac{\partial f(x,y)}{\partial x}&=\xi \cdot e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}\\

\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial x^2}&=\xi ^2\cdot e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}\\

\end{aligned}$$

Similarly,

$\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial y^2}=\eta ^2\cdot e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}$

Now, as given

$a \frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial x^2}+b\frac{\partial^2 f(x,y)}{\partial y^2}=f(x,y)$

or

$a \times \xi ^2\cdot e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}+b \times  \eta  ^2\cdot e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}= e^{(\xi x+\eta y)}$

$a\cdot \xi ^2+b\cdot \eta ^2=1$

Thus,

$\xi =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2a}}, \eta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2b}}$

$(\xi =\frac{1}{\sqrt{a}}, \eta = 0)$ and $(\xi =0, \eta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{b}})$ satisfy the above result.

Therefore, the correct option(s) are **A, B**.

for $l_n \leq x \leq 2l_n$

detailed_solution.concept: Communication Systems - Information Theory and Coding
detailed_solution.markdown: Channel capacity, $C_s=Max[I(X:Y)]$ $I[(X:Y)]=H(Y)-H\left ( \frac{Y}{X} \right )$ Where, $H\left ( \frac{Y}{X} \right )=-\sum_{i=1}^{3}\sum_{i=1}^{3}P(x_i,y_i) \log_2P\left ( \frac{y_i}{x_i} \right )$ $$P\left ( \frac{Y}{X} \right )=\begin{matrix} &y_1 & y_2 & y_3\\ x_1 &1-\alpha & \alpha & 0\\ x_2 &0 &1-\alpha &\alpha \\ x_3 & \alpha & 0 & 1-\alpha \end{matrix}$$ For simplication convenience, let $[P(X)]=[1\;\;0\;\;0]$ $$\begin{aligned} [P(X,Y)]&=[P(X)]_d\cdot \left [ P\left ( \frac{Y}{X} \right ) \right ]\\ [P(X,Y)]&=\begin{bmatrix} 1-\alpha & \alpha &0 \\ 0& 0&0 \\ 0 & 0 &0 \end{bmatrix}\\ H\left ( \frac{Y}{X} \right )&=-((1-\alpha ) \log_2 (1-\alpha )+\alpha \log _2 \alpha )\\ I(X:Y)&=H(Y)+(1-\alpha ) \log_2 (1-\alpha )+ \log _2 \alpha \\ C_s&=MAX\left \{ (X:Y) \right \}\\ &=MAX\left \{ H(Y)+(1-\alpha ) \log_2 (1-\alpha )+ \log _2 \alpha \right \}\\ &=log_2 3+(1-\alpha ) \log_2 (1-\alpha )+\alpha \log _2 \alpha \end{aligned}$$ Plot of $(1-\alpha ) \log_2 (1-\alpha )+\alpha \log _2 \alpha$ $C_s$ will be maximum at $\alpha =0$ and 1. Given $\alpha \in [0.25,1]$ Hence, $\alpha =1$ is correct answer. Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

Consider a channel over which either symbol $x_A$ or symbol $x_B$ is transmitted. Let the output of the channel Y be the input to a maximum likelihood (ML) detector at the receiver. The conditional probability density functions for Y given $x_A$and $x_B$ are:

$f_{Y|x_A}(y)=e^{-(y+1)}u(y+1),$
$f_{Y|x_B}(y)=e^{(y-1)}(1-u(y-1)),$

where $u(\cdot )$ is the standard unit step function. The probability of symbol error for this system is _________ (rounded off to two decimal places).

detailed_solution.markdown: ML decoding $\rightarrow \; f_{Y/X_A}(y)\underset{\overset{ \lt }{X_B}}{\overset{X_A}{ \gt }} f_{Y/X_B}(y)$ $i.e. \;\; f_{Y/X_A}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_B}(y) \rightarrow \text{ Decision favor of }X_A$ $i.e. \;\; f_{Y/X_A}(y) \lt f_{Y/X_B}(y) \rightarrow \text{ Decision favor of }X_B$ For $-1 \lt y \lt 0$ and $1 \lt y \lt \infty \rightarrow f_{Y/X_A}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_B}(y)$ For above internal decision in favor of $X_A$ For $-\infty \lt y \lt -1$ and $0\lt y \lt 1 \rightarrow f_{Y/X_B}(y) \gt f_{Y/X_A}(y)$ For above internal decision in favor of $X_B$ $P_e=P(X_A)\cdot P_{eX_A}+P(X_B)\cdot P_{eX_A}$ $P_{eX_A}\rightarrow$ Probability of error $X_A$ transmitted $P_{eX_B}\rightarrow$ Probability of error $X_B$ transmitted $P_{eX_A}=\int_{0}^{1} f_{Y/X_A}(y)dy=\int_{0}^{1}e^{-(y+1)}u(y+1)dy= \int_{0}^{1}e^{-(y+1)} dy=e^{-1}-e^{-2}=0.23$ $P_{eX_B}=\int_{0}^{1} f_{Y/X_B}(y)dy=\int_{0}^{1}e^{(y-1)} [1-u(y-1)]dy= \int_{0}^{1}e^{(y-1)} dy=e^{-1}-e^{-2}=0.23$ $P_e=P(X_A) \times 0.23+P(X_B) \times 0.23 =0.23[P(X_A)+P(X_B)]=0.23$ Therefore, the correct answer is **0.235** (acceptable range: [0.22, 0.25]).

ec:2022:ga:q9.title: GATE EC 2022 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 9
ec:2022:ga:q9.question:
In a class of five students P, Q, R, S and T, only one student is known to have copied in the exam. The disciplinary committee has investigated the situation and recorded the statements from the students as given below.

Statement of P: R has copied in the exam.
Statement of Q: S has copied in the exam.
Statement of R: P did not copy in the exam.
Statement of S: Only one of us is telling the truth.
Statement of T: R is telling the truth.

The investigating team had authentic information that S never lies.
Based on the information given above, the person who has copied in the exam is

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Facts & Statements:**
  - Exactly one of the five students $\{P, Q, R, S, T\}$ copied in the exam.
  - We are given that **$S$ never lies** $\implies$ Statement of $S$ is **TRUE**.
  - **Statement of S:** *"Only one of us is telling the truth."*
  - Since $S$ is telling the truth, $S$ is that unique truth-teller.
  - Therefore, all other four students ($P, Q, R, T$) are **lying (making false statements)**.

- **Deducing the Copier from False Statements:**
  - **Statement of T:** *"R is telling the truth."*
    - Since $T$ is lying, this statement is false $\implies$ $R$ is indeed lying (consistent with our premise).
  - **Statement of R:** *"P did not copy in the exam."*
    - Since $R$ is lying, this statement is false.
    - Negating *"P did not copy"* yields:
      $$\mathbf{P \text{ copied in the exam}}$$
  - **Statement of P:** *"R has copied in the exam."*
    - Since $P$ is lying, this is false $\implies$ $R$ did not copy. (Consistent!)
  - **Statement of Q:** *"S has copied in the exam."*
    - Since $Q$ is lying, this is false $\implies$ $S$ did not copy. (Consistent!)

- **Conclusion:**
  - The unique student who copied in the exam is **$P$**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (P)**.

ec:2022:ga:q10.title: GATE EC 2022 | Set 1 | GA | Question: 10
ec:2022:ga:q10.question:
Consider the following square with the four corners and the center marked as P, Q, R, S and T respectively.

Let X, Y and Z represent the following operations:
X: rotation of the square by 180 degree with respect to the S-Q axis.
Y: rotation of the square by 180 degree with respect to the P-R axis.
Z: rotation of the square by 90 degree clockwise with respect to the axis perpendicular, going into the screen and passing through the point T.

Consider the following three distinct sequences of operation (which are applied in the left to right order).
(1) XYZZ
(2) XY
(3) ZZZZ

Which one of the following statements is correct as per the information provided above?
options: The sequence of operations (1) and (2) are equivalent
The sequence of operations (1) and (3) are equivalent
The sequence of operations (2) and (3) are equivalent
The sequence of operations (1), (2) and (3) are equivalent

detailed_solution.markdown:
- **Given Operations on Square $PQRS$ (Clockwise: $P \to Q \to R \to S$):**
  - **Operation X:** $180^\circ$ 3D rotation about the $S-Q$ diagonal axis.
    - Keeps vertices on the $S-Q$ diagonal ($S$ and $Q$) fixed in their positions.
    - Swaps the other two vertices across the diagonal ($P \leftrightarrow R$).
    - Flips the face of the square (front to back).
  - **Operation Y:** $180^\circ$ 3D rotation about the $P-R$ diagonal axis.
    - Keeps vertices on the $P-R$ diagonal fixed.
    - Swaps the other two vertices across the diagonal.
    - Flips the face of the square back (back to front).

- **Evaluating Sequence $XY$:**
  - Start with initial configuration: Top-Left $= P$, Top-Right $= Q$, Bottom-Right $= R$, Bottom-Left $= S$ (Front face).
  - After $X$: Top-Left $= R$, Top-Right $= Q$, Bottom-Right $= P$, Bottom-Left $= S$ (Back face).
  - After $Y$ applied to the result of $X$:
    - Vertices on $P-R$ diagonal (Top-Left $= R$, Bottom-Right $= P$) remain in place.
    - Vertices on $S-Q$ diagonal swap: Top-Right becomes $S$, Bottom-Left becomes $Q$.
    - Face flips back to Front face.
  - Final configuration after $XY$:
    $$\text{Top-Left} = R, \quad \text{Top-Right} = S, \quad \text{Bottom-Right} = P, \quad \text{Bottom-Left} = Q \quad (\text{Front face})$$
  - Notice that every vertex has shifted two positions clockwise: this is an in-plane **$180^\circ$ rotation**.

- **Evaluating Operation Z & Sequences:**
  - **Operation Z:** $90^\circ$ clockwise in-plane rotation about the center $T$.
  - Two applications ($ZZ = Z^2$) yield a $90^\circ + 90^\circ = 180^\circ$ in-plane rotation.
  - Thus, **$XY$ is exactly equivalent to $ZZ$**.
  - **Sequence (1) $XYZZ$:**
    $$XYZZ = (ZZ)ZZ = Z^4 = 360^\circ \text{ rotation} = \text{Identity (leaves square unchanged)}$$
  - **Sequence (2) $XY$:**
    $$XY = 180^\circ \text{ rotation} \neq \text{Identity}$$
  - **Sequence (3) $ZZZZ$:**
    $$ZZZZ = Z^4 = 360^\circ \text{ rotation} = \text{Identity (leaves square unchanged)}$$

- **Comparing the Sequences:**
  - Sequence (1) and Sequence (3) both result in the **Identity transformation** ($360^\circ$ rotation).
  - Therefore, sequence (1) and sequence (3) are equivalent.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option B (The sequence of operations (1) and (3) are equivalent)**.
